name: Carpus Dead
description: Carpus Dead is a small barren world whose surface tells the story of repeated failed attempts at habitation. Dead riverbeds wind between dust seas like the tendons of a limp wrist, their banks lined with petrified vegetation from a natural biosphere that collapsed long before any colonist arrived. The terrain is flat and featureless across most of the surface, broken only by the skeletal remains of terraforming towers that stand at regular intervals like the bones of a hand stripped of flesh.

The thin atmosphere carries enough dust to create ruddy sunsets but not enough to breathe. The wind is constant and low, a mournful sound that moves through the failed terraforming equipment with a hollow resonance. The petrified vegetation crumbles at a touch, releasing dust that smells faintly of organic decay despite being millions of years old. The landscape has the exhausted quality of a body that has tried and failed to sustain life too many times.

A colonial settlement was established here three times over two centuries, each attempt ending in failure from different causes: equipment malfunction, supply chain collapse, and finally a structural failure during a dust storm that killed most of the third colony's population. The ruins of all three settlements are still visible, layered atop each other in a grim archaeological record of persistence and defeat. Microbial life from the first colony has survived in the soil around the terraforming equipment, slowly dying as its engineered environment degrades.

Carpus Dead serves as a cautionary tale in colonial planning, its failures studied in detail by those who hope to avoid repeating them. The water ice deposits identified by the first survey remain accessible and are the planet's only resource of real value. The surviving microbes represent the last living legacy of the colonization efforts, and their gradual extinction is being monitored by a remote sensing platform that constitutes the planet's only active infrastructure.
